prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Create exactly ONE repainted character illustration, true transparent RGBA background.

INPUT PRIORITIES:
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and absolute authority for camera, pose, perspective, anatomy projection, head orientation, expression, character identity and action composition. Work directly from this original red-haired archer image. Repaint its character; do not redesign its pose. Image 2 is ONLY the Sdorica / 万象物语 painted material and shape-language reference. Do not copy image 2's pose, white hair, character, costume silhouette, lettering, small chibi figure or backdrop.

HIGHEST PRIORITY — PRESERVE IMAGE 1'S PROJECTED ACTION:
Keep the ground-level upward-looking slightly tilted camera and the same fierce adult female archer at full draw. Preserve her face's three-quarter orientation toward the viewer, focused amber eyes, jaw and neck angle; do not turn her into a profile portrait.
Keep the original screen positions and overlap order of head, shoulders, pelvis, knees, ankles and hands. The large near thigh and gold-armored shin project toward the camera through the lower-right foreground, terminating in the dramatically oversized foreshortened foreground boot. This leg projects OUT OF THE PICTURE PLANE, not sideways across it. The small far boot remains tucked under and behind the pelvis near the lower middle-left, its knee folded low to the left. The implied ground contact and body weight remain legible even after removing the environment. The pelvis is supported by that folded rear leg, the torso rises and twists, and the near leg overlaps the pelvis in depth. Preserve the original perspective size ratios, compact torso, depth compression and strong diagonal action. Do not recenter, straighten, flatten, symmetrize or spread the pose. Do not turn this into a floating seated squat, jump, kneeling display or standing character sheet.
The draw hand anchors beside her cheek, rear elbow to the left; the bow hand and straight holding arm extend toward the right in the original projection. One coherent arrow at full draw, physically coherent bowstring, natural hands and joints. Keep the original close dramatic framing; do not shrink the character just to fit a bow tip or ponytail. Do not add a ground slab to explain the pose.

REPAINTING:
Use the refined hand-painted fantasy illustration language of image 2: designed continuous color areas, graceful structural edges, selective fine drawing, soft volume transitions inside broad shapes, restrained textured brushwork only where it supports form. Preserve the archer's rich crimson hair, deep purple clothing and warm gold metal identity. Saturated but controlled, warm clear skin, expressive hand-drawn facial features. The face has the greatest care and clearest focal contrast.
Light the whole figure coherently from the upper right/front: a connected bright head-and-shoulder region, quieter torso and lower body. Broad matte and satin midtone surfaces support a FEW concentrated luminous highlights at the head edge and selected metal turns. Allow a small clean highlight bloom near the head that fades into alpha. Keep metal recognizable with shaped reflections on broad curved planes, not scattered silver/gold patchwork. No continuous glowing outline around the whole figure.

HAIR:
Retain image 1's high ponytail root and vigorous sweep upward and to the left, with the same overall action direction and relative volume. Organize it into connected overlapping masses that gradually taper and merge; a clear outer silhouette and restrained internal strand indications. The light belongs to the whole hair volume. Avoid separately illuminated little strands, flyaway frizz, thin loops, shredded tips, equal-width coils, tubular plastic locks, piled ribbon curls and alternating bright/dark stripes. Keep red saturation through the matte midtones.

CLOTHING AND ARMOR:
Preserve the figure and broad purple/gold identity while editing the outfit into a coherent wearable design. Connected fitted purple torso garment, short waist-fastened overlapping skirt panels and curved articulated gold light armor; clean shoulder/upper-arm and upper-thigh exposure. Every cloth panel has an understandable seam or belt attachment. Keep only a small number of overlapping cloth shapes behind the hips, flowing with the motion and ending around the thighs. Remove the long central hanging strip and detached left/right trailing cloth; no extra leggings or purple shorts layer across the exposed thighs. Keep adequate non-explicit coverage. Do not carry forward the later drafts' silver breastplate and floating squat. Metal plates have broad intact surfaces and selective decorative accents, not jagged spikes or tiny tessellated facets. Purple cloth keeps one continuous local color with a few stress folds and soft broad shading, not faded patches or triangular lighting shards.

DELIVERY:
Exactly one character, no scenery, no castles, rocks, dust cloud, background wash, black rectangle or checkerboard baked into pixels, no text or chibi. Actual transparent background. Crisp clean cutout edges with natural painted edge variation, no grain fringe. Preserve image 1's powerful camera and action first, then apply the material/shape treatment. This is a fresh repaint FROM IMAGE 1, not a continuation of any later generated archer draft.
